prompt: A school play sold $10^3$ tickets at $\$8$ each. Putting on the play cost the school $\$1{,}500$. How many dollars does the school have left after paying the costs?
hint: Try smaller numbers first: $10^1 = 10$ tickets at $\$8$ is $\$80$, and if costs were $\$30$ you would have $80 - 30 = \$50$ left. Turn the power of ten into a plain number, multiply, then subtract — exactly the same three moves.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try smaller numbers first: $10^1 = 10$ tickets at $\$8$ is $\$80$, and if costs were $\$30$ you would have $80 - 30 = \$50$ left. Turn the power of ten into a plain number, multiply, then subtract — exactly the same three moves.
First rewrite $10^3$ as a regular number, then find the money taken in, then subtract the costs.

explanation: Step 2 — money taken in: $1{,}000 \times \$8 = \$8{,}000$, because multiplying by $1{,}000$ adds three zeros to the $8$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: A very common wrong answer is $\$8{,}000$ — the money taken in, with the costs never subtracted.
Another is treating $10^3$ as $30$ (multiplying the base by the exponent), which gives $30 \times 8 = 240$ and a nonsense total.
$10^3$ means $10 \times 10 \times 10 = 1{,}000$, and the word "left" tells you a subtraction still has to happen: $8{,}000 - 1{,}500 = 6{,}500$.
